pr_title: Bluetooth: Mesh: Add proxy send callback
pr_body:
Zephyr Bluetooth Mesh did not check whether the proxy message
was actually sent out, so that the response message could
not be received during reset. It did not solve the status
callback of the proxy sending message, so a new problem was
introduced after PR(#28457) merged.

bt_mesh_prov_send(&buf, public_key_sent))

This PR will try to solve the above problem, and will fix
the problem due to thread competition, and PR(#26668) will
not be necessary.

Compared with PR(#30138), it no longer consumes extra RAM
space and supports synchronization of group addresses

This is a resubmission of PR(#32666)

Fixes #36100. 

Signed-off-by: Lingao Meng <menglingao@xiaomi.com>
pr_comments: @LingaoM looks generally good, but I'd suggest adding some more meat to the bones in the first commit message, since right now it's just repeating the short commit summary.

issue_context.title: pb_gatt buf_send does not call callback
issue_context.body:
I am provisioning a BT Mesh device that is set up as a PB Gatt device. Provisioning is failing because the OOB input_complete message is never received when inputting an alphanumeric OOB value. The provisioner device times out after 60 seconds of not receiving the input_complete message. This is because the callback 'public_key_sent' is never called for PB Gatt devices when sending the public key. 

In commit 4cc8cb1c1513033e8aa6d9c1086456a062c9bc57 the 'public_key_sent' callback is added to manage flags to make sure that 'send_input_complete' isn't called before the public key is sent. The flag that specifies that the public key was sent never gets set and that flag is checked before calling 'send_input_complete()'. PB Gatt function 'buf_send' takes a callback as input but does nothing with it, causing the PUB_KEY_SENT flag to never get set.

To fix, 'buf_send' in pb_gatt.c should call the callback argument if one exists

This is a show stopper as I can not provision my PB Gatt device
comments: Hi, PR https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/35702 is fixing this problem.

review_comments:
I believe this should happen before the callback, so that this buffer becomes available for reuse in the callback. 
This requires this function to make a copy of the `BT_MESH_ADV` structure first though.

I'm a little worried about `BT_MESH_ADV(buf)->data` may be modified elsewhere.

Because of `send_end_cb` can be processed by app layer, and app layer may block the current process. If other processes apply for buffer at this time, `cb_data` may be overwrite?
Yes, it's not the adv pointer that's passed, it's the content.
Why not add `&& adv->started` to the `if` in `bt_mesh_adv_send_end` instead? It seems like it would be slightly easier to follow. This, and the `if (started)` in the destructor could be removed.
There's no need for this if anymore
We should deal with the error situation. What do you mean?

Riiight, I see. I was thinking that the `started` flag should only be set if the advertising could actually be started, ie, it did not return an error. This works as well though, so I'll approve, and leave it to you :)
This looks wrong to me since `buf_send()` doesn't call `net_buf_ref()`

Yes that makes more sense. And I hope it's more to your taste too: reference counting can be an ample source of bugs, so following some basic principles when using it makes the code more predictable and understandable.

The removal of this line holds the connection state open making the provisioner believe the radio is busy. When reinstated the changes work great and appear to speed up the entire provisioning process.

Simple change: bt_mesh_adv_send_end(err, BT_MESH_ADV(buf));
I see what you are trying to do but it does not close connections cleanly. If I put the implicate end calls back in it works fine.
